facts.summary: Positive Phase 2 time-averaged Lp(a) reduction data presented at AHA, no safety concerns · Phase 2 · zerlasiran in ASCVD with high Lp(a) · not yet approved
facts.indication: atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with high lipoprotein(a)

evidence.summary: Results presented today showed that zerlasiran (300 mg every 16 weeks, 300 mg every 24 weeks or 450 mg every 24 weeks) produced greater than 80% mean time-averaged placebo-adjusted reductions from baseline in Lp(a) concentrations over 36 weeks.
evidence.safety: reductions in Lp(a) persisted and no safety concerns emerged with infrequent dosing.
evidence.program_discontinued: We look forward to progressing zerlasiran into Phase 3 as a potentially promising new treatment for patients with high Lp(a).
